answer_text: The Eight Mechanical Faults of Enema Nozzles (Ashta Netra Dosha) and associated complications: 1. Hrasva (too short nozzle): Medicine fails to traverse the rectal sphincters and flows back externally without therapeutic action. 2. Dirgha (too long nozzle): Nozzle reaches too deep into upper rectum or sigmoid, risking mechanical perforation or mucosal laceration. 3. Tanu (too narrow orifice): Fluid delivers too slowly or clogs with herbal paste (Kalka), prolonging procedure and causing tenesmus. 4. Sthula (too thick nozzle): Causes severe anal sphincter overstretching, tearing, mucosal abrasion, and excruciating pain. 5. Jirna (old or cracked nozzle): Rough edges scratch the mucosal lining, predisposing to sepsis and fistula formation. 6. Parshwa-chhidra (side holes instead of terminal orifice): Medicine sprays obliquely against the rectal wall, causing localized trauma. 7. Vakra (bent nozzle): Enema fluid is directed asymmetrically, creating painful rectal spasms. 8. Asamyak-karnika (improper protective ring): Nozzle slips excessively deep into rectum during administration.
